title: Canonical source reductions intertwine semilinear quotient transitions
statement: Fix finite-field and coefficient data D,C,E and separated finite-type schemes X,Y over D.k. Let f:X -> Y be smooth separated of pure relative dimension d, and let K be integral constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Put U=Lf* K(d)[2d]. Let b_n: L_n U -> U_n be the specified source reduction of [def-pur-adic-source-reduction], and let tau_(m,n):U_m -> Res_(m,n) U_n be the adjoint of the independently specified root-normalized finite-source comparison of [def-pur-adic-finite-source-normalization]. Let t_(m,n)(U) be the actual integral reduction transition of [def-pur-integral-reduction-transitions]. For every n <= m, b_m;tau_(m,n) = t_(m,n)(U);Res_(m,n)(b_n). This is only the quotient compatibility square, with no finiteness, invertibility or cocycle assertion.

proof.text: Compute tensor by the integral Tate line on a flat-term K-flat representative. The normalized line reduction square sends (x tensor u) tensor v to x tensor q(u)v in either order. The root quotients commute with the direct quotient, so the scalar-unit-normalized transposes of these maps agree. The bijective scalar adjunction identifies this with the actual adicPurityTwistReduction.

Its root-normalized comparison is exactly the normalization fixed in def-pur-adic-finite-source-normalization. Transpose the resulting direct-quotient square to the semilinear equation, using the prescribed restriction identification.

theorem purAdicSourceReduction_transition_square
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource C.l E Y))
    (hK : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral C.l E Y K) {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    purAdicSourceReduction D C E f d K hK m ≫
        purAdicFiniteSourceTransition D C E f d K hK h =
      normalizedDVRReductionTransition C.l E X D C.different h
          (purAdicSource D C E f d K) ≫
        (normalizedDVRRes C.l E X h).map (purAdicSourceReduction D C E f d K hK n)
